title: A Vocabulary of the Korwa language
author: William Crooke
publication: Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal 61(1):125–128
catalog_year_note: Biodiversity Heritage Library catalogs this volume/article as 1893; the article running head and volume contents print 1892.
reuse_basis: The Biodiversity Heritage Library states for this exact article: Copyright Status: Public domain; the BHL considers that this work is no longer under copyright protection. The original article was printed in 1892. Four rendered source pages and extracted lexical facts are kept with attribution; the full journal PDF remains a local temporary audit cache.
source_lect: Korwa, from one bilingual Korwa speaker among families in the southern part of Mirzapur as stated by Crooke; no precise village or coordinates supplied
scope: Crooke's entire four-page glossary, printed pp. 125–128; on p. 128 only the 13 lines above the rule and W. H. P. Driver's separate article
visual_recheck: 20 page-stratified printed lines checked against saved page images on 2026-09-25 (six each from pp. 125–127, two from p. 128); 19 selected and one held line, zero material accepted-form errors; see visual-sample-20260925.jsonl
overlap_policy: The independent Crooke attestation of lutur 'ear' is retained despite exact matches in Bahl 1962 and Pinnow 1959; no evidence that Crooke copied either later source. Driver's adjacent p. 128 comparison is not part of Crooke's glossary and supplies no installed rows.
transcription_policy: Forms preserve Crooke's printed romanization and diacritics as visually checked. No unattested IPA is inferred. Hindi/Sanskrit/English comparisons are kept as source notes rather than etymology edges. Inflected verbs, multiword expressions, disjunctive or uncertain glosses are held.
graph_policy: No etymology graph edges inferred from Crooke's casual Kuri, Hindi, Sanskrit or English comparisons.
